text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Albanian President Sali Berisha's praise of U.S. President Bill Clinton's commitment to NATO's eastward expansion is an attempt to patch up relations with the United States after the recent friction between the two countries, the newspaper editorial says.
- The trial of an Albanian who threatened to blow himself up with a bomb unless he could meet President Sali Berisha was postponed because of an absence of witnesses.
- Two smaller parties have blamed the main opposition Socialists for their own losses in Sunday's local elections.
- Bulgaria's prosecutor general rejected a decision of the Foreign Minister to discharge the ambassador to Albania, Stefan Naumov, according to a Bulgarian newspaper.
- Hungary has donated 100,000 polio vaccines to Albania.
- US AID signed an agreement with the Bank of Albania to assist its stock exchange.
- An Albanian woman, aged 30, died in a speedboat accident as one of a group attempting to enter Italy illegally.
- The first foreign player in Albanian soccer history, the Brazilian Edu, scored his first goal.
- Albania's appeal court upheld the jail sentences of four Albanians accused of forming a communist party in breach of the constitution.
- Jailed Socialist leader Fatos Nano is calling for a staff shake-up at the opposition daily newspaper Zeri i popullit.
- An Albanian replaced his friend, who emigrated abroad, in the army and is being paid 10,000 leks monthly.
- The ethnic Greek Human Rights Party blamed the refugees' non-participation in the local elections for its loss in southern Albania.
- Former head of the secret police Sigurimi Irakli Kocollari and another senior official Vladimir Hysi are to go on trial for destroying files of the former secret police.
